title: Choose the clean official direction
question: These options follow your steer: official, easy to use, clean, and not overly decorative.

options.label: Privacy Clearance Sheet
options.lineage: ISO calibration certificates, accredited lab reports, and inspection dockets
options.thesis: Every masking run reads like a clear inspection: five checks enter, one privacy-safe result leaves.
options.viewport: A single precise work sheet fills the screen: source and protected specimens align side by side, five checks form a narrow rail, and the primary action certifies the result.
options.risk: Can feel too administrative unless the transformation remains visibly immediate.

options.label: Industrial Privacy Labels
options.lineage: equipment labeling, stockroom wayfinding, and safety tags
options.thesis: Literal labels make every private-data zone and state unmistakable.
options.case: Clear and direct; fuses poorly with official trust when hazard stripes dominate.
options.viewport: A white working field uses bold quoted labels for source, result, and five rules, with one orange inspection tag marking the active state.
options.risk: Fashion and warehouse references can feel louder than the requested tone.

options.label: Compliance Terminal
options.thesis: Every input, rule decision, and protected output prints into one auditable transcript.
options.case: Strong technical identity; fuses poorly with Thai-first ease and clean official presentation.
options.viewport: One keyboard-first transcript shows source, selected rules, processing state, and protected output in a continuous ordered record.
options.risk: A terminal-first interaction is less approachable for nontechnical viewers.

canonCard.label: Clean compliance dashboard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar, official two-panel masking tool with restrained styling.
canonCard.viewport: Compact title bar, source editor, protected output, five checkboxes, and one prominent action.
canonCard.risk: Highly usable, but less distinctive during the presentation.
